Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade two
Subject: General
Strand: Transport Suggested vocabulary fly, float, road, rail, water, air, tarmac, fast,
Topic 3.1: Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and vocabulary
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and vocabulary, part of Transport Suggested vocabulary fly, float, road, rail, water, air, tarmac, fast, in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade two General.

Key inquiry question: Why should we listen attentively when other people are talking?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication: The learner’s ability to listen keenly and actively is enhanced as they the learner listens attentively and responds

appropriately to two-directional instructions.

20

• Learning to learn: The learner’s ability to work independently is enhanced as they practise saying words with the target letter-sound

combinations correctly.

Values:
Respect: Acceptance is achieved as the learner understands and appreciates others during group discussions.

Link to

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills: The learner’ self-esteem is nurtured as they are able to read words with the target letter sound combinations correctly.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Attentive listening is emphasized in Kiswahili and Indigenous Language Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Assistive technology such as universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, weighted pencil/pen grips, page-turners, adapted digital devices

Other Related Service Providers: Resource person, speech therapist, Learner support assistance, Occupational Therapist, Physiotherapist.
